requirement_quote: The following health and welfare conditions, where applicable to the unit, must be listed in the VHWP (see standard H 1.4): a) metabolic disorders (hypocalcaemia, hypomagnesaemia, ketosis, displaced abomasum, bloat, acidosis)
reasoning: Names ketosis as a condition the VHWP must list. Under H 1.4 (PDF 45, printed 43) the VHWP must record the level of each listed condition for the farm, set a threshold limit and monitor it, which is a record of cases, so it names the clinical case incidence. The clause says ketosis without clinical or subclinical; subclinical ketosis is read from tests (I021, I022) and no test is named. how_checked is records_review: listed, recorded and monitored in the VHWP, a farm record. No number; H 1.4 e) leaves the threshold to the farm. The justification document (PDF 9, printed 7) names ketosis among production diseases the transition cow standards address. Rule 4 check: H 1.5 says where applicable to the unit; this follows whether the condition occurs on the farm, as any record of cases does, and is not limited to a housing type, a target or an optional module, so it is read as applying to every certified farm. Rule 5: the condition named without its form names this clinical incidence row only. Rule 11: H 1.4 requires the level to be recorded and monitored.

Not required under rule 11. Ketosis is named only in the treatment protocol standard: "The Herd Health Plan (HHP) includes a written protocol for treatment of the following common diseases: diarrhea, displaced abomasum (DA), ketosis, mastitis, milk fever, metritis, pneumonia, and any additional routinely occurring diseases identified by the veterinarian." (Chapter 4, Treatment of Common Diseases, PDF 56). A treatment protocol alone does not name a case measure. The Treatment Records standard (Chapter 2, PDF 24) requires records of each treatment of "the facility's common diseases" with the "Disease/condition being treated", but it names no condition itself, so it does not count either. Searched every page for a requirement to record, monitor or report cases of the condition and found none; FARM's evaluation of the protocol standard reviews treatment records (PDF 56), which is a check, not a requirement to record cases. Both standards are related practice requirements.

No sensor or automated data is mentioned for these counts. Rule 11: the standard requires the farm to report cases of the named condition. The frequency "every other month" is recorded (rule 13). Related: 6.B.21, all Steps (PDF 40, printed 30), close-up cow diets adjusted "to reduce the incidence of metabolic diseases associated with calving (e.g., udder edema, laminitis, ketosis, milk fever etc.)", a practice.

requirement_quote: Body condition scoring must be: a) undertaken at least four times per year at the following times during a cow’s production cycle: i. drying off ii. calving iii. 60 days post-calving iv. 100 days prior to drying off b) recorded in the VHWP for animals with scores below 2.0 or above 4.0.
number_in_requirement: at least four times per year; 60 days post-calving; 100 days prior to drying off; below 2.0 or above 4.0
reasoning: Names body condition scoring with numbers. how_checked is records_review: b) says scores below 2.0 or above 4.0 are recorded in the VHWP, so the assessor checks recorded scores. Other requirements: H 4.1, body condition change planned, maintained and recorded in the VHWP (PDF 50, printed 48); H 4.3, the nutrition plan must say how BCS <2 and BCS ≥4 animals will be managed (PDF 50, printed 48); M 3.4 b), stock keepers must know body condition scoring (PDF 33, printed 31). In the Welfare Outcome Assessment (WA 1.1 a), Appendix 4 item 2, PDF 97, printed 95) the assessor visually scores 20 randomly selected cows as thin, moderate or fat on the Defra condition scoring method, which is visual_inspection. The RSPCA scale is the Defra 1 to 5 scale, not the Welfare Quality 0 to 2 scale.

requirement_quote: Lactating Cattle: 99% or more of lactating cows observed have a body condition score of 2 or greater on FARM Body Condition Scorecard.
section: Chapter 9: Animal Observations, Body Condition; FARM Body Condition Scorecard
number_in_requirement: 99% or more of lactating cows observed have a body condition score of 2 or greater
reasoning: Required. The standard makes the FARM Body Condition Scorecard (PDF 146 and 147) binding, so section names both (rule 3); it applies to the lactating cows of every certified farm (rules 4 and 6). Names body condition score with a number. FARM's scorecard for post-weaned heifers and cows runs 1 to 5 (PDF 147) and for calves 1 to 3 (PDF 146), described in words. The same page sets 99% or more at score 2 or greater for pre-weaned calves and weaned heifers. How checked, PDF 148: "Observation: Observe and score animals to determine if the benchmark is met for each age class."
